item: About thirty GET routes that run heavy work, reach out, or mint a key now refuse a request another site's page makes (R278); monitoring/health no longer counts a kill-switch refusal as down
summary: The Origin middleware only checks state-changing methods, so any page the person visits could fire a GET at the loopback address: the in-memory rollup benchmark (the #1310 crash class), the other benchmarks and selftests, /all, the hazard and source-health fetches, the Wikipedia dump probes, and the custody and annotation exports that mint a signing key. src/api/cross_site.py holds the backup route's own check (Host, Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin or Referer) as one dependency; 28 routes carry it. A foreign Origin, Origin: null or cross-site Fetch Metadata is answered 403 before the handler runs; no Origin still reaches it. Stated limit: a browser sending no Fetch Metadata for a referrer-less img still gets served and cannot read the answer. database.py's private copy is Export's to repoint later; making the routes POST stays a proposal. W1: summary.down in monitoring/health counted a probe the airplane switch refused as the source being down; it is now refused_by_kill_switch.
